glossary.definition: One credential that is the agent's whole identity in the registry: scopes, custodian, caps, expiry, guardrail and grants hang off it. The agent sends it as a Bearer token on every call. The VirtualKey is server-generated and cannot be edited.
The human an agent acts as and answers for. If the custodian's account goes inactive the key stops working, so pick someone who will stay.
A policy that lets a key reach one app, optionally only some tools. It references the key by NAME, not by its value.

There is no rotate endpoint. Snapshot the spec, create a successor under a new name, copy its grants, verify it with a call, then revoke the old key. A PUT carrying a new VirtualKey returns 200 and is ignored.
Revoked:true. The only non-destructive kill: the key, its caps and its grants stay, and the gateway answers 401 without saying why.
The upstream provider key an llm-scoped agent key needs at create time. Reads return it as an empty string, so deleting an llm key before holding the RealKey is a one-way door.
A key with no static secret that authenticates by a token from an external issuer, with a mandatory audience and a lifetime cap. Whether the deployed gateway accepts these tokens is UNVERIFIED.

sources.title: RFC 6750: The OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Usage
sources.use: Bearer credential and the 401 challenge shape

cards.label: Register, grant, call
cards.description: One key is the agent's whole identity: scopes, custodian, caps and expiry hang off it. The grant is what lets it reach one tool.

cards.label: Revoke and watch it refused
cards.description: Revoke is the only non-destructive kill. The key, its caps and its grants stay; the gateway answers 401 and does not say why.

cards.label: Two different 403s
cards.description: Two different 403s. A missing scope names itself; a missing grant is a bare 403 that only the gateway log explains.

cards.label: The 429 shape
cards.description: Caps are registration attributes on the key. Over the cap the gateway answers 429 with retry-after; waiting clears it. Enforcement policy belongs to the kill-switch demo, not this one.

cards.label: Rotate by replacement
cards.description: A PUT with a new VirtualKey returns 200 and changes nothing. Real rotation is snapshot, create successor, verify, revoke the old.

cards.label: The delete trap for llm keys
cards.description: Reads return RealKey as an empty string, so a deleted llm key cannot be recreated unless you hold the upstream key. Revoke instead.

cards.label: Same-name recreate inherits grants
cards.description: Grants reference keys by name. A new key with the old name silently inherits the old key's access, including access nobody reviewed for the new key.

cards.label: A workload identity with no secret
cards.description: The key trusts an external issuer instead of holding a secret. The audience is mandatory and the token lifetime is capped. Gateway acceptance on the real product is UNVERIFIED.

cards.label: Expiry and renewal
cards.description: An expired key is refused like an unknown one. Moving NotAfter forward renews it, so put every expiry on a calendar.

cards.label: Traps that cost hours
cards.description: RealKey, same-name grants, the PUT that is ignored.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.

stories.title: Register, grant, call: the agent gets its own identity
stories.say: One key is the agent's whole identity: scopes, custodian, caps and expiry hang off it. The grant is what lets it reach one tool.

stories.title: Revoke the agent and the gateway refuses it
stories.say: Revoke is the only non-destructive kill. The key, its caps and its grants stay; the gateway answers 401 and does not say why.

stories.title: Deleting an llm key without its RealKey is a one-way door

stories.title: Delete and recreate under the same name: grants come back
stories.say: Grants reference keys by name. A new key with the old name silently inherits the old key's access, including access nobody reviewed for the new key.

stories.title: Expiry retires an agent on its own, and editing renews it
